prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1352; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you state your full name for the record?

A: Sorry, I'd rather keep my name off the recording for now. You can use the claim number.

Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?

A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, Texas, heading toward the east side of town. I had just gotten into the right lane to make a turn.

Q: Was there anything unusual about traffic at that moment?

A: Not really. It was moderately busy, but moving steadily. I checked my mirror, saw the lane looked clear, and started to change over.

Q: What happened next?

A: A vehicle in the lane I was moving into clipped my passenger side as I merged. There was a scraping sound and my car jerked toward the shoulder. I got it under control, pulled over, and stopped.

Q: Did the other driver stop as well?

A: Yes, they pulled up a little ahead of me. We exchanged information and they seemed apologetic. They said they didn't see me coming.

Q: Were you hurt at the scene?

A: I felt okay right away, just a little shaken. But by the next morning my lower back was really tight and sore. It's a strain, I think. I've been having trouble sitting for long periods and bending over.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment since?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care and they told me it looked like a muscle strain. They gave me medication and told me to rest and do some gentle stretching. I'm following up with my own doctor this week.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I was driving carefully and I believe the other driver should have seen me. I'm hoping this can be resolved without too much hassle.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
